claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high mechanical strength at room temperature.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high mechanical strength near 1000 °C.
Replacing Hf completely with Nb yields NbMoTaTiZr.
Replacing Hf with Nb will reduce the alloy density.
NbMoTaTiZr will retain mechanical strength similar to HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature.
NbMoTaTiZr will retain mechanical strength similar to HfMoTaTiZr at approximately 1000 °C.
Suitable processing can produce a predominantly single-phase BCC NbMoTaTiZr microstructure.
The Nb-substituted alloy will have lattice distortion comparable to that of HfMoTaTiZr.
Nb has roughly half the atomic mass of Hf.
Nb is a refractory element with a high melting point.
The lower atomic mass of Nb relative to Hf is the mechanism by which substitution reduces overall alloy density.
Nb and Hf have reasonably comparable atomic radii.
Lattice distortion contributes to solid-solution strengthening in these alloys.
Preserving lattice distortion after Nb substitution will preserve room-temperature and elevated-temperature mechanical properties.
Complete Nb substitution may reduce density by approximately 10–15%.
The hypothesis is restricted to room-temperature through approximately 1000 °C mechanical loading and to microstructures without detrimental secondary phases.
Long-term phase stability, oxidation behavior, and precipitation kinetics after Nb substitution are uncertain.
A greater than 15% decrease in room-temperature or 1000 °C strength relative to the identically processed baseline would falsify the mechanical-property-preservation prediction.
Development of secondary phases that compromise mechanical properties would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention permits either complete or partial Hf replacement, but the named product and experimental design specify NbMoTaTiZr, which corresponds to complete replacement. A partial replacement would retain Hf and require a different, explicitly quantified composition.
